title: Base change shifts the delta-dimension of every irreducible component by the constant c
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-setup-base-change, for X -> S locally of finite type and X' -> S' the base change, the lemma asserts that if X is integral with dim_delta(X) = k then every irreducible component Z' of X' has dim_{delta'}(Z') = k + c (statement lines 15138-15144). The proof uses that X' -> X is flat, being a base change of the flat S' -> S (Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat), so every generic point x' of an irreducible component of X' maps to the generic point x of X by lifting of generalizations along flat morphisms (Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-generalizations-lift-flat) (proof lines 15146-15153). Writing s for the image of x in S, it views x' as a point of S'_s x_s x, which is a monomorphism into S' x_S X, and applies flatness of Spec(kappa(x)) -> Spec(kappa(s)) again to see that x' maps to a generic point s' of an irreducible component of g^{-1}(s), so delta'(s') = delta(s) + c by the assumption of the base change situation (proof lines 15155-15167). The fibre dimensions at x and x' agree by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change, both are generic points of the corresponding fibres, and the transcendence degrees of kappa(x) over kappa(s) and of kappa(x') over kappa(s') agree by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point, which gives the displayed equality delta_{X'/S'}(x') = delta(s') + trdeg = delta(s) + c + trdeg = delta_{X/S}(x) + c and hence the claim by Definition labelled definition-delta-dimension (proof lines 15169-15179). Transporting the generic point through the two flat maps and comparing fibre dimensions and transcendence degrees is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
